name: Respiratory variants & flu
value: Early US flu season; EU still at baseline
summary: US flu admission rate highest for the time of year since 2010-11; England saw early signs; EU at baseline
state: US hospitals logged 6,100 flu admissions in the week to 24 Oct, with the estimated rate the highest for that week since 2010-11; the CDC forecasts a likely rise to the week ending 14 Nov, and H1N1 is dominant (Nature World News, 4 Nov). UKHSA reported on 8 Oct that September flu activity in England was above the past four winters, while still at baseline. ECDC reported on 3 Nov that EU/EEA consultation rates remain low or at baseline, with no change to SARS-CoV-2 variant classifications. Health systems are not reported as strained.
for_you: Older people, young children and those with long-term conditions are most exposed. The NHS and UKHSA publish flu vaccination guidance, and US readers can check CDC advice.
rubric_hit: Watch: a hemisphere's flu season unusually early (US rate highest for week 42 since 2010-11); no WHO variant of concern, health systems not strained

sources.title: Nature World News — CDC forecasts flu hospitalizations will likely keep climbing through mid-November
UKHSA — Flu levels low at start of season but higher than previous 4 years

why: Known viruses change; a new COVID-19 variant or a severe flu strain can strain health systems without being 'novel'.
drivers: Viral evolution, waning immunity, seasonal patterns, vaccine match.

rubric.alert: WHO designates a variant of concern, or flu or COVID-19 hospitalisations strain several countries' health systems.
rubric.watch: WHO designates a new variant of interest, or a hemisphere's flu season is unusually early or severe.
rubric.normal: No WHO variant of interest rising fast; flu seasons of normal severity.
